correctness.rationale: For the real cubic Day--James norm, the sphere consists exactly of same-sign cubic arcs, opposite-sign taxicab facets and nonsmooth axes. On a cubic arc, the unique norming functional fixes the Birkhoff--James partner; for t<=1/2 one norm exceeds 4/3, while for t>=1/2 the cubic expression 1+F(t) has F strictly decreasing to F(1)=3/2^(4/3), established by the explicitly positive H(t) bound. Taxicab partners are forced to the cubic diagonal and give the same sharp value only at their midpoint. At axes the complete supporting-functional interval yields strict lower bounds >4/3. The balanced unit pair attains both norms equal to (1+3/2^(4/3))^(1/3). The analytic stratum split and inequalities prove the continuum claim; independent SymPy identities and 1250 numerical configurations only corroborate it.
residual_risks: Results only for exponent 3 and real scalar field; no extension to other Day--James exponents.
Finite diagnostics do not independently prove the universal inequality; analytic proof was separately reconstructed.

final_claim: For the real cubic Day--James plane X=ell_3--ell_1, the Birkhoff--James orthogonal Schäffer infimum g_perp(X) equals the exact radical (1+3/2^(4/3))^(1/3), attained at x=(2^(-1/3),2^(-1/3)) and y=(1/2,-1/2) and norm symmetries. No statement for general p.
